passages.provision_quote: The Secretary of the California Health and Human Services Agency shall research, develop, and pursue discussions of a waiver framework in consultation with the federal government with the objective of creating a health care system that incorporates the following features and objectives:
passages.note: The operative sections direct research, stakeholder engagement, a draft waiver framework and reports to the Legislature; they establish no coverage and no financing.
Wiener is listed in the Ayes on concurrence, 29-9, so the vote is not near-unanimous, but the bill he voted for is a research-and-report directive.
passages.actor_quote: Ayes Allen, Archuleta, Ashby, Atkins, Becker, Blakespear, Bradford, Caballero, Cortese, Dodd, Durazo, Eggman, Gonzalez, Laird, Limón, McGuire, Menjivar, Min, Newman, Padilla, Portantino, Roth, Rubio, Skinner, Smallwood-Cuevas, Stern, Umberg, Wahab, Wiener

rows.reasoning: SB 770 (2023-2024), which Wiener authored and voted for, orders the Health and Human Services Secretary to "research, develop, and pursue discussions of a waiver framework" and to deliver interim and final reports, so it is a study-and-report directive and no passage survives V4. The legislative endorsement of "a health care system with unified financing, such as a single-payer health care system" sits in Section 1000's findings and declarations, which the operative section governs over, and the framework it describes still contemplates cost sharing outside essential services and a sliding-scale income contribution, so it does not match "Make healthcare free and available to everyone, fully paid for by the public sector" clause for clause.
